name: Arthur-Pieman Conservation Area
reason: Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania name it; wild beaches, Sandy Cape Track and visitor centre (rule 1-2).
objection: Overlaps Edge of the World and the Tarkine as a larger area; keep only as the wider area with its own beaches/4WD.

name: Boat Harbour Beach
reason: Wikivoyage names the turquoise little bay as a stop; second-tier beach, always there.
objection: One-line mention; short visit.

name: Cradle Mountain
reason: Iconic summit named by Wikivoyage, Discover Tasmania; day walk from Dove Lake.
objection: Part of the national park spot; distinct enough as the headline peak and summit climb.

name: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park
reason: Flagship World Heritage park, Wikivoyage, Parks Tasmania, Discover Tasmania.
objection: Likely a destination, not a spot; placement decides, not inclusion.

name: Devonport
reason: Gateway city with its own Wikivoyage chapter: Mersey Bluff lighthouse and penguin viewing, Tiagarra cultural centre, Don River Railway (rule 1-2).
objection: The Wikivoyage See list is thin; its draws are individual spots, so the city may suit a destination or be a low-rank gateway rather than a spot.

name: Dove Lake
reason: Glacial lake under Cradle Mountain with the 6 km loop track; named by Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania.
objection: Part of the Cradle Mountain area; but a distinct place and walk.

name: Edge of the World
reason: Wikivoyage names it as the signature stop on the west coast; coastal cliffs/viewpoint, free, always open.
objection: Small viewpoint inside Arthur-Pieman; near-duplicate risk if the conservation area also listed (distinct stop though). Wikipedia article is a redirect (0 views).

name: Gunns Plains Caves
reason: Show cave (guided tours) named by Wikivoyage Ulverstone/Penguin chain and tourism sources; a real half-hour+ visit.
objection: Local feeling; only two counted sources.

name: Lake St Clair
reason: Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania: Australia's deepest lake, visitor centre at Cynthia Bay, ferry and walks.
objection: Page views (63038) and the wiki title/coordinates belong to the North American Lake St. Clair (candidate coords are in Michigan): fix wiki to the Tasmanian article ('Lake St Clair (Tasmania)') and recheck coordinates; part of the national park spot.

name: Latrobe
reason: Historic town with Gilbert Street heritage, Axemans Hall of Fame and platypus viewing; only one real-sourced listing (Wikivoyage Latrobe (Tasmania) page); town itself is a modest draw.
objection: Case for: Wikivoyage chapter and Axemans Hall of Fame is a named attraction (that should be the spot). Against: a town wrapper, the attraction is the spot.

name: Mole Creek Karst National Park
reason: Only Tasmanian park protecting caves (Marakoopa and King Solomons guided tours); Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania.
objection: Park vs separate cave spots may overlap.

name: Mount Roland
reason: Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania: peak with 360-degree summit walk above Sheffield.
objection: Strenuous full-day walk; wiki title points at conservation area.

name: Narawntapu National Park
reason: National park with Wikivoyage entry and Parks Tasmania; wildlife (wombats, wallabies) and beaches.
objection: Only a small park; wildlife seen at dusk.

name: Overland Track
reason: Australia's most famous multi-day walk, Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania; fee/booking system, season.
objection: Linear feature inside the national park; a trail with a pin at midpoint, not duplicate of park.

name: Penguin
reason: Seaside town with the Big Penguin icon, heritage trail and beach; Wikivoyage lists it only as 'home of the Big Penguin', no town page.
objection: Case for: quirky roadside icon (Big Penguin) is a recognised stop. Against: the town itself has a short visit; weekly market excluded; the icon should be the named spot.

name: Pool of Bethesda
reason: Wikipedia article and 96143 views and coordinates (31.78, 35.24) are for the biblical pool in Jerusalem, not the Tasmanian tarn; the real tarn is only a passing mention in Wikivoyage's park page, part of the Walls of Jerusalem walk.
objection: A genuine named tarn on the Walls of Jerusalem circuit, but it is part of the larger park/walk spot with one passing mention.

name: Rocky Cape National Park
reason: Parks Tasmania, Wikivoyage; coastal walks, caves and lighthouse-style headland views.
objection: Small park, modest visits.

name: Sheffield
reason: Town of Murals: permanent large murals, named by Wikivoyage Western Tasmania and Discover Tasmania; the town itself is the draw (rule 3).
objection: Wikivoyage page candidate resolves to Sheffield UK; the Tasmanian town has no own page, only list mention; Mural Fest is an event and excluded.

name: Somerset Beach
reason: Wikivoyage Burnie and Western Tasmania: swimming beach along Somerset coast, but the pin is the Somerset town centre point.
objection: Case for: a beach that guides name. Against: ordinary suburban-style beach, short visit, no distinct draw; coordinates and wiki are the town's.

name: Stanley
reason: Historic fishing village with visitor centre, Highfield Historic Site, penguin viewing and the Nut; Wikivoyage page.
objection: A town beside The Nut; the Nut is separate, but the streets/Highfield are the town's own draws.

name: Table Cape
reason: Wikivoyage Wynyard and Western Tasmania: headland lookout and lighthouse; free.
objection: Tulip bloom is seasonal event; outside spring it is a short lookout stop.

name: Takayna / Tarkine
reason: Named by Discover Tasmania as a wilderness region of rainforest and coast; a region, not one place.
objection: Case for: widely promoted draw. Against: a regional label overlapping Arthur-Pieman, Edge of the World and Trowutta; no single place to stop; may be a destination.

name: The Nut
reason: Volcanic plug with chairlift and 4.6 km summit circuit, Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania.
objection: Beside Stanley town; distinct.

name: Ulverstone
reason: Wikivoyage page lists only cafes, a volunteer-run history museum and surrounding sites (Lillico Beach, Leven Canyon); the town has no own draw.
objection: Case for: fifth-largest city with its own Wikivoyage chapter. Against: its See entries are outside the town; a town is a spot only if the town is a draw.

name: Walls of Jerusalem National Park
reason: World Heritage park with multi-day and day walks, Wikivoyage and Parks Tasmania.
objection: Remote, demanding walk.
